description: Machine-readable catalog of data-collection capabilities exposed by the Solo Agency Local Collector. AI agents in playbooks read this list to decide which capability fits a user's request, then submit a collector job whose source specifies the chosen capability id plus inputs. The collector runs the matching extractor and returns typed records. Facebook screens use the internal-GraphQL provider (richer, structured); every other site falls back to generic HTML extraction. Collection is read-only and runs only under the user's explicit command on accounts and pages the logged-in user can already access.

usage.how_agents_choose: Match the user's intent against each capability's 'when_to_use' and 'output_schema'. Prefer a Facebook GraphQL capability whose status is 'stable' or 'beta'; if none fits, submit the source without a capability id and the collector applies generic HTML extraction.
usage.how_to_invoke: POST /jobs/run_now with sources[] where each source is { "url": "<screen url>", "capability": "<capability id>", "inputs": { ... } }. Read results from the run's private_data_points.jsonl; typed output is in the record's 'records' field, keyed by the capability's output_schema.
usage.orchestration_note: Multi-step work (visiting many profiles, friend-of-friend traversal, filtering by industry, writing reports) is the playbook agent's job. Each capability only reads ONE screen into typed data.
usage.status_meaning: stable=live-verified; beta=unit-verified, live pending; planned=not built; not_graphql=this screen is not served by GraphQL interception (server-rendered / interaction-gated) and needs a DOM/HTML approach or an alternative capability.
usage.pagination: Deep collection via cursor replay: set inputs.max_pages (default 8, max 40) on any paginated capability (group.posts, group.search_posts, groups.search, people.search, profile.posts, profile.friends, newsfeed). Instead of relying on scroll to load more, the collector replays the captured query with each end_cursor to pull further pages directly. Example: fb.group.search_posts with max_pages:10 returned 66 posts vs 6 without.

PostRecord.engagement: object { reactions, comments, shares } | null — counts when visible, null when not surfaced

ProfileSummary.name: string

ProfileSummary.industry_hint: string | null — coarse hint if surfaced on the row

AboutRecord.contact: object — public contact fields the profile shares

ReelRecord.creator: { name, url } | null — the reel author
ReelRecord.caption: string — visible caption text (includes creator name + hashtags)
ReelRecord.hashtags: array of #tags parsed from the caption

WebResult.title: string
WebResult.url: string — real destination url (empty for ads)

ProfileHeader.name: string
ProfileHeader.category: string — e.g. Realtor / Real Estate Agent
ProfileHeader.website: string — external site link when shown
ProfileHeader.cta: array of button labels (Book Now, Send Message, ...)
ProfileHeader.intro_bio: string — the profile's own blurb, when it has one
ProfileHeader.work: string[] — employers the profile declares (Works at / Worked at / Làm việc tại)
ProfileHeader.intro_lines: string[] — the intro card lines as written, capped at 20. READ THESE to work out a trade: `category` is a narrow hard-coded whitelist (real-estate and insurance wording only) that is blind to every other job and can false-positive on a page that merely mentions the words.

ReactionResult.status: string — done | already | dry_run | not_found | redirected | no_match | ambiguous_match | listing_unavailable | unresolved_match | error
ReactionResult.reaction: string — like | love | care | haha | wow | sad | angry
ReactionResult.verified: boolean — reaction confirmed present after the click
ReactionResult.target_preview: {author, snippet, url} — so the report can confirm the right post
ReactionResult._match_fields: when the job named its target by match_text, the MatchOutcome fields are merged into this record

CommentResult.status: string — done | dry_run | not_found | redirected | no_match | ambiguous_match | listing_unavailable | unresolved_match | error
CommentResult.text: string — the comment that was posted
CommentResult.verified: boolean — composer cleared after submit (post confirmed)
CommentResult.appeared: boolean — the text was found in the on-page comment list
CommentResult._match_fields: when the job named its target by match_text, the MatchOutcome fields are merged into this record

MatchOutcome._note: Merged into a Comment/Reaction result when the job named its target by CONTENT (match_text) instead of by permalink. The match is made in code, never by the agent: exactly ONE hit is required — 0 or >1 writes NOTHING and returns no_match / ambiguous_match.
MatchOutcome.matched_post: {url, text, post_id, created_time, from} — the post that was acted on. `from` is graphql | dom (see sources_read).
MatchOutcome.candidates_considered: number — distinct posts read from the listing (duplicates across captures/replayed pages are collapsed first)
MatchOutcome.candidates: [{url, text, created_time, from}] — on no_match the posts that WERE read; on ambiguous_match the colliding hits. This is the audit trail for a refusal: it shows the resolver actually read the feed.
MatchOutcome.sources_read: {graphql, dom} — how many posts each source supplied. TWO sources are merged on purpose: Facebook server-renders the TOP of a feed into the first document and only FETCHES older pages, so the GraphQL intercept is systematically blind to the NEWEST posts — the ones most worth acting on. Measured on a live group, graphql=2 (older posts) while the newest post was on screen the whole time and only the DOM source saw it. The DOM half comes from filtering.js, which pairs each permalink with its BODY and stops at the first comment boundary; a hand-rolled scan was tried first and attached a commenter's words to the post instead.
MatchOutcome.match_text: string — the needle that was searched for
MatchOutcome.list_capability: string — the listing extractor used (fb.group.posts | fb.profile.posts | …)
MatchOutcome.resolved_from: string — the listing url the job pointed at
MatchOutcome.listing_url: string — where the search actually ran

ProfileDossier.name: string
ProfileDossier.category: string — Facebook's own label when it has one. NARROW: only real-estate/insurance wording is ever recognised, so an empty category means nothing.
ProfileDossier.work: string[] — EMPLOYERS parsed from 'Works at <X>'. Measured on 5 live profiles: EMPTY on all five, because Facebook writes 'Realtor at the Carlbrook Group', not 'Works at ...'. Do not rely on this field; read about_lines.
ProfileDossier.location: string[] — Lives in / From, parsed from the intro card. Often EMPTY even when the location is plainly stated: Pages print it as a bare city line ('Garden Grove, CA') or inside the Work section ('Boca Raton, Florida'), neither of which matches the 'Lives in <X>' pattern. Read about_lines for the real answer — same as with industry, the collector supplies the signal and the agent decides.
ProfileDossier.intro_lines: string[] — intro card lines as written, capped at 20
ProfileDossier.about: object — the text each About surface added, keyed by the SLUG actually found on the page (contact_info, work_and_education, basic_info, links, ... — Facebook names them differently on Pages vs personal profiles, so the keys vary). Only surfaces that opened appear. Each value is that surface's NEW lines; furniture repeated on every tab is not restated. Read about_lines rather than keying off a specific tab name.
ProfileDossier.about_lines: string[] — every about.* line flattened in visit order, capped at 120. READ THIS to work out the trade: 'Loan Officer at Wells Fargo' lands here, and the title is what separates Loan & Mortgage from Banking & Financial. The employer alone does not.
ProfileDossier.emails: string[] — published addresses found anywhere in the walk. Measured empty on all five test profiles, and no directory_contact_info tab appeared on any of them: absence of a contact tab is absence of published contact data, not a collector failure. Read `discovered_tabs` before concluding an address does not exist.
ProfileDossier.websites: string[] — outbound links published on the profile
ProfileDossier.website: string — the single best external site
ProfileDossier.cta: string[] — button labels (Book Now, Get Quote, View Shop, ...) — weak corroboration for retail vs service
ProfileDossier.found_on: string|null — which surface the first address came from
ProfileDossier.checked: string[] — surfaces that actually RENDERED, in visit order. The audit trail: never conclude email_not_found or 'no trade stated' unless this shows the ladder ran.
ProfileDossier.missing: string[] — surfaces that WERE discovered and then failed to open, or that the budget cut off. A surface the profile simply does not publish is absent from discovered_tabs instead: found-then-lost and never-offered are different facts and are not merged.
ProfileDossier.budget_exhausted: boolean — true when the internal deadline stopped the walk early; the record is partial and `missing` says what was skipped
ProfileDossier.discovered_tabs: string[] — EVERY About sub-nav slug found on the page, including ones the walk skipped. The slugs are a fixed vocabulary (/<profile>/directory_<section>). Empty means no About links were found at all — a code or layout problem, not an empty profile.
ProfileDossier.graphql_by_surface: object — the GraphQL queries each surface fired, keyed like `about`: {surface: [{query, doc_id}]}. Read this to find out whether a surface can be REPLAYED instead of clicked: one named query per surface means it can be called by doc_id the way fb.profile.hovercard calls CometHovercardQueryRendererQuery, and the tab-clicking goes away. With probe_graphql:true each row also carries `variables` (truncated to 900 chars) and `has_fb_dtsg` — the token's PRESENCE, never the token.
ProfileDossier.see_more_expansions: number — how many truncated 'See more' blocks were expanded across the whole walk. The collector's own expansion runs once, on the entry page, before this capability is injected; this one runs per surface, so a bio cut off inside a sub-tab is no longer lost.
ProfileDossier.about_panel_found: boolean — true when every line came from the About card itself. false means the panel was not located and the text is whatever the main column held, posts and reviews included. A dossier assembled from a timeline reads exactly like one assembled from an About section; this flag is the only thing that tells them apart, so distrust about_lines when it is false.

ContactRecord.emails: string[] — published addresses found on the profile
ContactRecord.websites: string[] — outbound links published on the profile (usually from directory_links). Use these for the website hop instead of re-scanning.
ContactRecord.found_on: string|null — current_page | directory_contact_info | directory_intro | directory_basic_info | directory_links; null when nothing was found
ContactRecord.checked: string[] — surfaces that actually RENDERED, in visit order. May also contain "about" (the ladder entered the About section). This is the audit trail: never conclude email_not_found unless it shows the ladder ran past current_page.

MessageResult.recipient: string — the name on the open thread, proven to match recipient_name
MessageResult.verified: boolean — composer emptied AND the message appeared
MessageResult.requested_id: string — the profile id / vanity the job asked for (the identity anchor)
MessageResult.open_id: string — the id actually in the address when the action started
MessageResult.id_verified: boolean — requested_id was still the open thread BEFORE the E2EE gate was touched. This is the primary identity proof. false is NOT an accusation: once a thread is encrypted Messenger rewrites /t/<profile_id> to /t/<thread_id>, and from the url a legitimate rewrite and a wrong thread look identical — so false only means the anchor was unavailable and the NAME had to decide instead.
MessageResult.name_matched: boolean | null — whether the open thread's name equals recipient_name; null when no recipient_name was given. Informational when id_verified is true (people rename themselves); decisive when it is false.
MessageResult.title_check: string — match | mismatch | unavailable | unchecked. The page title independently names the thread on messenger.com ("<Name> | Messenger"). "unavailable" = the title carried no name (facebook.com/messages); "unchecked" = no recipient_name was supplied. Neither is a failure.
MessageResult.recipient_title: string — the name read from the page title, when there was one
MessageResult.passed_e2ee_gate: boolean — a pre-encryption thread needed its Continue button clicked first
MessageResult.thread_url: string — the e2ee thread url after the gate

GroupPostResult.text: string — the post body that was submitted
GroupPostResult.group: string — the group id actually posted into
GroupPostResult.group_url: string — the url at submit time
GroupPostResult.verified: boolean — true only for status done: the composer closed AND the text appeared
GroupPostResult.closed: boolean — the composer dialog closed (the submit was consumed)
GroupPostResult.appeared: boolean — the text was found on the page afterwards
GroupPostResult.approval_notice: string | null — the group's own wording when the post is held for admin approval

HovercardRecord.id: string — the profile id asked for
HovercardRecord.name: string
HovercardRecord.context: string[] — the card's context lines AS WRITTEN ("Works at X", "15 mutual friends including …"). Read these; they are the only part that says what someone does.
HovercardRecord.work: string[] — context lines that matched a work prefix
HovercardRecord.actions: string[] — the card's buttons (Message / Add friend / Follow), which reveal the viewer's relationship to this person

capabilities.title: Facebook group posts (feed)
capabilities.when_to_use: Read recent posts from a Facebook group the logged-in user can access — for lead scanning, idea mining, or monitoring discussion inside a group.

inputs.max_scroll: int (optional) — how many feed pages to load
inputs.max_pages: int (optional, default 8, max 40) — deep pagination via cursor replay
inputs.within_days: int (optional) — keep only posts newer than N days. Omit for no time limit.
inputs.since: string|int (optional) — ISO date or unix seconds; keep posts at or after this.
inputs.until: string|int (optional) — ISO date or unix seconds; keep posts at or before this.
inputs.include_undated: bool (optional, default false) — a post whose timestamp could not be read cannot be judged against the window. It is EXCLUDED by default and always COUNTED in time_window.undated; set true to keep it.

capabilities.coverage: logged-in user's accessible view of the group

_impl.time_window: Filtering happens AFTER extraction and never stops pagination early. Group SEARCH results are ranked by relevance, and a group FEED sorted by RECENT_ACTIVITY floats an old post the moment someone comments on it — so "I saw something older than the window, therefore the rest is older" is false on both surfaces. The bound on work is max_pages. The result carries time_window {since, until, within_days, excluded_older, excluded_newer, undated, undated_kept} and page_cap_hit: with a window, page_cap_hit is the difference between "nothing else in range" and "the walk ran out of budget", which a short list alone cannot tell you.

capabilities.title: Facebook profile About / bio
capabilities.when_to_use: NOT AVAILABLE — do not submit jobs with this capability. Use fb.profile.header (category, follower count, website, CTA), fb.profile.contacts (published email/websites) and fb.profile.posts (what the person actually posts about) instead; together they cover profile classification.
capabilities.coverage: only fields the profile makes visible to the logged-in user

_impl.history: Twice attempted, twice withdrawn. A DOM implementation walking About + its four directory_* sub-tabs could not finish inside the orchestrator's 45s capability timeout even after the settle time was cut and a wall-clock budget added; both runs returned records:null. Removed on operator instruction — the other profile capabilities already carry enough to classify a person, and this one cost more than it was worth.
_impl.what_it_exposed: Its failures were INVISIBLE, and fixing that was the durable win: a DOM capability that threw used to answer available:false, which the bridge turns into records:null — making "the capability crashed" and "this page has nothing" the same output. That path now reports available:true with the error, catches promise rejections as well as synchronous throws, and background.js writes an explicit error record instead of leaving null.
_impl.if_revived: Do not walk five surfaces in one job. Fetch is useless here (the SPA shell has no rendered block), so each surface costs a real click plus a settle; either split the ladder across jobs or raise the capability timeout deliberately.

capabilities.title: Facebook post comments
capabilities.when_to_use: Read the comments on a specific post — for mining leads or sentiment from a discussion thread.

inputs.post_url: string (required) — a permalink to the post

capabilities.output_schema: { post: PostRecord, comments: [{ author: EntityRef, text, created_time }] }
capabilities.coverage: comments visible to the logged-in user

_impl.finding: 2026-07-15: no comment GraphQL query fires on a passive permalink scroll. The first page of comments is server-rendered (initial document/RSC payload); only load-more PAGINATION uses GraphQL (CometUFICommentsProviderQuery), which needs enough comments to trigger. capabilities.title: Facebook Reels feed (creator + caption + hashtags)
capabilities.when_to_use: Collect people from the Reels feed by industry: the agent reads each reel caption/hashtags to detect a trade (real estate, insurance, mortgage, ...) and collects the creator. NOTE: DOM-driven (creator/caption are NOT in GraphQL) — it advances the Reels player and scrapes each displayed reel.

inputs.reel_url: string (required) — a https://www.facebook.com/reel/<id> to enter the feed
inputs.max_reels: int (optional, default 20, max 80) — how many reels to advance through and scrape
inputs.debug: bool (optional) — include a DOM sample for tuning

_impl.method: DOM: advance player via ArrowDown + scroll, scrape reel-link cards for creator link + caption text + hashtags
_impl.note: GraphQL FBUnifiedVideoContainerQuery paginates reel URLs but carries NO caption/creator (deferred render module, confirmed across 16 chunks), so this is DOM-based.
_impl.validated_on: 2026-07-17 absellsaz/reels/ → 60 reels with views (2.8K…190K) via grid mode
_impl.grid_mode: profile reels TAB (/…/reels/) → scrape a[href*="/reel/<id>"] cards: reel_id + view count overlay (parseCount) + url; infinite-scroll, stop after 2 dry scrolls. Player mode (/reel/<id>) still advances + scrapes caption/creator.

capabilities.title: Web search (DuckDuckGo / Google / Bing) — result links + snippets
capabilities.when_to_use: Search the OPEN WEB (beyond Facebook) for a query — a person, email, business, or topic — and get organic result links + titles + snippets. Use to find someone's public web presence (personal site, social profiles, listings, directories) for enrichment, or general research. Ads are filtered out by default.

inputs.url: string (required) — the search engine results URL. DuckDuckGo (default, safest): https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q=<enc>. Google (richer, but higher CAPTCHA risk at volume — use for targeted enrichment): https://www.google.com/search?q=<enc>. Bing: https://www.bing.com/search?q=<enc>. The extractor auto-detects the engine by host.
inputs.include_ads: bool (optional, default false) — keep sponsored results too

capabilities.coverage: public web search results (DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint)

_impl.method: DOM, engine auto-detected by host: DuckDuckGo (.result rows, uddg-decoded url), Google (external a[href] wrapping an h3 — robust to class churn), Bing (li.b_algo). Ads filtered.
_impl.note: DuckDuckGo HTML chosen for clean, parseable markup + low bot-detection vs Google. First result page only (no pagination yet). To read a RESULT PAGE's content, submit its url with NO capability — the generic HTML engine returns readable text (raw_visible_text_excerpt).
_impl.validated_on: 2026-07-16 (live DDG 10 results; Google DOM parses 9 organic in in-app browser)
_impl.engines_note: DuckDuckGo default = clean markup + low bot-detection (best for bulk). Google = best coverage but can trigger 'unusual traffic' CAPTCHA when hit at volume; prefer for low-volume, high-value lookups. Runs in the user's real logged-in Chrome, which lowers (but does not remove) that risk.

capabilities.title: Facebook profile/page header (followers, verified, website, CTA)

capabilities.coverage: the logged-in user's view of the public profile/page header

_impl.method: DOM/SSR (no clean GraphQL header query, like About): text patterns for 'N followers'/'N likes', verified marker, category words; first external non-FB link = website; /reels + /videos link presence; CTA from role=button labels.
_impl.note: Server-rendered; robust to class churn by keying off text/links. One record = the profile.
_impl.validated_on: 2026-07-16 discovery on absellsaz (followers 10K, verified, Realtor, hasReels confirmed in DOM)

capabilities.title: Read Facebook's hover preview card for one profile
capabilities.when_to_use: Cheap per-person enrichment: the card Facebook shows when you hover a name. Returns the context lines the profile itself declares ("Works at X", "Studied at Y", "Lives in Z"), plus gender, verified and avatar — one request per person, no page navigation. Use it to SIFT a large list (fb.profile.friends gives you the entity ids) before spending fb.profile.header / fb.profile.contacts on the few worth a full look. It does NOT return a trade or a title: read `context` and decide.

inputs.entity_id: string (required) — the numeric profile id. fb.profile.friends returns it for every friend.
inputs.debug: bool (optional) — include the raw user/context node skeletons for shape work

capabilities.coverage: what the hover card shows the logged-in operator

_impl.screen: any Facebook page (the call is made from whatever page is open)
_impl.graphql_query: CometHovercardQueryRendererQuery — issued directly, no hover needed. Found by hovering three profiles and diffing the capture buffer: the ONLY varying input is entityID.
_impl.doc_id: taken from Facebook's own module registry via window.require("<QueryName>.graphql").params.id so it can never go stale; a measured value is the last-resort fallback.
_impl.auth: fb_dtsg/av borrowed from any request the open page already made
_impl.fields: context[] is the payload's timeline_context_items rendered as text, kept RAW alongside the parsed work/education/location split — the split keys off English/Vietnamese prefixes, and anything that does not match a prefix would otherwise vanish.
_impl.limits: Only what the card shows. A person who declares no workplace yields an empty context, and an employer name alone often does not reveal a trade ("Works at Caliduadon llc"). For trade classification prefer fb.profile.header's intro_lines + website.

capabilities.title: React to a Facebook post/video/reel (like, love, …)
capabilities.when_to_use: WRITE ACTION. Add a reaction (default love/like) to a single post, video, or reel. Submit the post PERMALINK as the url — or, when you only know what the post SAYS, point the url at the group/timeline and pass match_text (see fb.post.comment; the resolution is identical). Approval is handled upstream by the daily report — only create this job for content the operator has approved. Idempotent: if the post is already reacted, it is left unchanged.

inputs.post_url: string (required) — permalink: /watch/?v=, /<user>/posts/<id>, /permalink.php?..., /reel/<id>, story_fbid; OR a group/timeline url when using match_text
inputs.reaction: string (optional, default like) — like | love | care | haha | wow | sad | angry
inputs.match_text: string (optional) — identify the post by its CONTENT instead of a permalink. Same semantics as fb.post.comment.
inputs.match_mode: string (optional, default contains) — contains | exact | regex
inputs.dry_run: bool (optional) — locate + preview the target WITHOUT clicking (debug only; not the approval gate)

capabilities.coverage: the logged-in operator reacts as themselves via the real UI

_impl.method: DOM automation (MAIN world, gql_actions.js): locate the main post UFI react toggle by locale-aware aria-label (EN+VI); for a non-like reaction, hover to open the flyout and click the option; real pointer+mouse event chain; verify via aria-pressed / Remove-label after click.
_impl.idempotent: if already reacted, no-op (clicking Like again would REMOVE it); P1 does not switch an existing reaction to a different one.
_impl.note: One action per job. Pacing/caps/approval live in the flow layer + daily report, not in this capability.
_impl.audit: result appended to outbox/actions_log.jsonl by the bridge
_impl.validated_on: 2026-07-17 real like on reel/4524074751166406 → done/verified; drift-guard + scrollSteps=0 for writes

capabilities.title: Comment on a Facebook post / video / reel
capabilities.when_to_use: WRITE ACTION. Post a comment on a single post, group post, or reel. Submit the post PERMALINK (a group post permalink works the same as a profile one). When you only know what the post SAYS and not its url, point the url at the GROUP or TIMELINE and pass match_text — the collector finds the post in code. Do NOT list the feed yourself and pick a url by eye: that is the judgement call this input exists to remove. Approval is handled upstream by the daily report — only create this job for content the operator approved.

inputs.post_url: string (required) — permalink: /watch/?v=, /<user>/posts/<id>, /permalink.php?..., /reel/<id>; OR a group/timeline URL when using match_text (or the older match_caption)
inputs.match_text: string (optional) — identify the target post by its CONTENT. The collector reads the listing with fb.group.posts / fb.profile.posts, filters IN CODE, and requires exactly one hit: 0 matches returns no_match and >1 returns ambiguous_match, and in both cases NOTHING is written. On a hit it navigates to that permalink and comments there, echoing matched_post + candidates_considered.
inputs.match_mode: string (optional, default contains) — contains | exact | regex. All are case-insensitive and whitespace-normalised; regex also accepts match_flags.
inputs.match_source: string (optional) — force the listing extractor (fb.group.posts | fb.profile.posts | fb.group.search_posts | fb.newsfeed) instead of inferring it from the url
inputs.match_max_pages: number (optional, default 3) — how many cursor pages of the listing to search before giving up
inputs.match_caption: string (optional, LEGACY) — in-page variant that scopes the action to a matching [role=article] on the CURRENT page. Prefer match_text: it resolves to a permalink first, so it cannot comment into a neighbouring post's composer.
inputs.dry_run: bool (optional) — locate composer + preview WITHOUT posting (debug only; not the approval gate)

capabilities.coverage: the logged-in operator comments as themselves via the real UI

_impl.method: DOM automation (gql_actions.js): find the composer by its aria-label prefix "Comment as …" (the same on post, group post and reel — a looser match also hit the search box); on a reel first click the [role=button] labelled exactly "Comment" and WAIT for the composer to render; type with execCommand insertText (Lexical accepts it); submit with Enter keydown/keypress/keyup; verify BOTH that the composer emptied AND that the text appears on the page.
_impl.match_text_flow: Two phases in one job. Phase 1 (__soloActResolve, a separate entry point that is structurally unable to write): the listing page is scrolled so Facebook fires its feed query, gql_extract's fb.group.posts / fb.profile.posts reads it, duplicates are collapsed by canonical permalink, and match_mode filters what remains. Phase 2 runs only on exactly one hit: background.js navigates the SAME tab to that permalink, re-injects, and comments there. It must NOT comment inline on the listing — a feed holds one "Comment as …" composer PER POST, so the first-match selector would land on the wrong one. The resolved permalink is re-checked against a host allowlist (facebook.com only, which excludes the l.facebook.com link shim) before the tab is navigated, and again in-page after the load, because the url comes from page-supplied data.
_impl.note: One comment per job. Pacing/caps/approval live in the flow layer + daily report.
_impl.audit: result appended to outbox/actions_log.jsonl by the bridge
_impl.validated_on: 2026-08-15 match_text live on group 668676178569386: resolved "Post 5 post 5 post 5" to /posts/676092881161049/ and commented there (done/verified); match_text "Post" returned ambiguous_match over 3 candidates and wrote nothing. Earlier, 2026-07-29 on all three permalink surfaces: profile post, group post, and reel (needed the panel-open click)

capabilities.title: Whole profile in ONE visit: header + every About tab (contact AND trade)
capabilities.when_to_use: The DEFAULT capability for enriching a person, and it replaces calling fb.profile.header and fb.profile.contacts on the same profile. Submit the profile's ABOUT url (https://www.facebook.com/<profile>/about) — landing straight there costs one page load instead of landing on the timeline and navigating. It reads the About overview plus five sub-sections: contact_info, work, education, intro, category. Read `about_lines` to decide what the person does; the JOB TITLE ('Loan Officer at Wells Fargo') is there, while `work` only ever holds the employer.

inputs.profile_url: string (optional) — defaults to the page the job opened; vanity or profile.php?id=<numeric>
inputs.budget_ms: int (optional, default 30000) — hard deadline for the About walk. The capability is killed at 45s, so raising this trades tabs-visited against losing the whole record.
inputs.settle_ms: int (optional, default 2800) — how long to wait for one tab's text to stop changing
inputs.probe_graphql: bool (optional, default false) — also record each captured query's variables and whether an fb_dtsg was present. Use when investigating whether a surface can be replayed by doc_id instead of clicked; leave off in production, the variables are large.

capabilities.coverage: what the logged-in operator can already see on the profile and its About section

_impl.method: reads the landing page first (name, category, followers, website, CTA, Intro card), then enters About and CLICKS every sub-tab in order: contact_info -> work_education -> intro -> basic_info -> links. Matches each tab by href slug (directory_* on Pages, about_* on personal profiles) and falls back to the visible label in English or Vietnamese. Keeps each tab's NEW text lines, not the whole page. Re-reads the header afterwards and unions work/education/location, because a line the main page truncated is often complete on a sub-tab.
_impl.note: NOT a classifier and must not become one. It returns what the profile says about itself as text; the reading agent picks the industry. Two keyword maps in this codebase already show why a fixed list here goes wrong: `category` only knows real-estate/insurance wording, and industryHint() only knows 14 trades — every other job is invisible to both.
_impl.differences_from_fb.profile.contacts: walks Work and education (contacts never did), never stops at the first email (contacts stops by default), and KEEPS the tab text (contacts ran two regexes over it and discarded the rest). fb.profile.contacts stays as-is for jobs that only want an address as fast as possible.
_impl.timeout: background.js kills a capability at 45s and an earlier version of this ladder (fb.profile.about) blew that twice and was deleted. Hence a 2.8s per-tab settle and an internal 30s deadline: when the budget runs out the walk stops and returns a PARTIAL record with `budget_exhausted: true` and the unvisited tabs listed in `missing`, rather than being killed and returning nothing.
_impl.known_limit: Superseded: 'See more' is now expanded on EVERY surface, not just the entry page, and the expansion happens before the harvest so the delta records the full line rather than the truncated one.
_impl.validated_on: 2026-08-15, five personal profiles on aven-ngo. The About sub-nav is really directory_{intro,work,education,category,personal_details,names,privacy_and_legal_info} — Work and Education are TWO tabs, and directory_work_and_education / directory_basic_info / directory_links do not exist. Discovery carried 4 of 5; the fifth failed to enter About and collected only its landing page. Whole walk 1865-11780ms against the 45s ceiling.
_impl.fallback: website/off-platform search when `emails` is empty and `checked` shows the ladder ran
_impl.replay_candidate: Every About surface is served by ONE query: ProfileCometAboutAppSectionQuery, doc_id 27470497829312569. Its section selector is NOT a constant, though: collectionToken is 'app_collection:pfbid...' and appSectionFeedKey is opaque, both minted per profile AND per section. So replay can remove the per-tab CLICKING but not the page visit — load the profile, enter About once, harvest every section token from that response, then fire the sections in parallel by doc_id.
_impl.sections: EVERY section the profile publishes, discovered from the sub-nav rather than guessed. Sections render in about a second each, so none are skipped. Order is still priority (contact_info, work, education, intro, category, then the rest) because the BUDGET can cut a very long sub-nav — losing Hobbies beats losing the address.
_impl.never_clicks: Anything inside a role=article/feed container. Every POST carries its own 'See more', so matching that label across the document expanded posts and reels instead of the bio — 5, 12 and 14 clicks on three live pages, pulling post text and reel view counts into the dossier as if they were profile facts.
_impl.reads_only: The About CARD, located by walking up from a directory_* sub-nav link. A Page's About url also renders Reviews, Posts, Photos and Related Pages below the panel, and blacklisting containers could not keep them out: role=article/feed does not match a Reviews card, so review text was harvested and each review's own 'See more' was clicked. Whitelisting the panel cannot be outflanked by a section type nobody anticipated. No panel found, no expansion at all.
_impl.infers_nothing: industry and location are the READING AGENT's call, from about_lines. The collector ships signals, never verdicts — the two regex classifiers already in this file (`category`, industryHint()) are what that rule was written from: one knows only real-estate and insurance wording, the other 14 trades, and every other job is invisible to both. A live profile stating 'NMLS# 342274' is a mortgage originator, and no keyword map in this file would have said so.

capabilities.title: Dig a Facebook profile for a published email/contact
capabilities.when_to_use: Find the address a business publishes on its OWN profile. Checks the rendered page (the collector expands "See more" first, which is where many bios hide the address) then the About sub-tabs in order: contact_info → intro → basic_info → links. Submit the profile URL. Only go to the website/off-platform ladder after this returns nothing.

inputs.profile_url: string (optional) — defaults to the page the job opened; vanity or profile.php?id=<numeric>
inputs.stop_at_first: bool (optional, default true) — stop at the first surface with an address; false = collect from all

capabilities.coverage: what the logged-in operator can already see on the profile

_impl.method: reads the rendered page text (background.js has already expanded "See more"), then enters About and CLICKS each sub-tab /<profile>/directory_{contact_info,intro,basic_info,links} (numeric: &sk=<tab>), waiting for the text to stop changing before reading. A same-origin fetch of those tabs returns the SPA shell without the contact block — across 68 profiles it yielded zero addresses — so they are never fetched. Then strips script/style, regex + junk-domain filter.
_impl.validated_on: 2026-07-28 bgvinvest (info@bgv.com.vn on all 5 surfaces) and Khanhngo.us (khanh8601@gmail.com on MAIN once "See more" expanded, and on contact_info; absent from intro/basic_info/links)
_impl.note: `checked` is the audit trail — do not conclude email_not_found unless the ladder actually ran.
_impl.scroll: NONE. The address lives in the bio and the four directory_* sub-pages, never further down a feed. Scrolling this job only queries posts that the contact task discards.
_impl.known_limit: "See more" expansion runs ONCE, on the entry page, before this capability is injected — it is not re-run on the sub-tabs. An address truncated inside a sub-tab can therefore be missed; a sub-tab miss is weaker evidence than a main-page miss.
_impl.audit_field: `checked`, not `opened_contact_tab`. `opened_contact_tab` is a generic pipeline flag that only fires when the JOB URL was already an about/directory URL, so it stays false on a normal profile-URL job even when the ladder ran correctly. Do not gate on it.

capabilities.title: Send a Messenger DM to one person
capabilities.when_to_use: WRITE ACTION. Send a direct message. The job url MUST be the THREAD — prefer https://www.messenger.com/e2ee/t/<vanity_or_profile_id>, which accepts a VANITY so no numeric-id lookup is needed first. NEVER the profile page. Identity is anchored to the PROFILE ID in that url, not to the display name, so a recipient who has renamed themselves still receives the message. Approval is handled upstream by the daily report.

inputs.thread_url: string (required) — PREFERRED https://www.messenger.com/e2ee/t/<vanity_or_profile_id>; also accepted: messenger.com/t/<id>, facebook.com/messages/t/<profile_id>. A profile url is rejected outright (not_a_thread_url), and so is any url that is not a real thread — a photo id, for example, opens a page with no composer at all.
inputs.recipient_name: string (OPTIONAL, was required before 0.1.71) — a display name is a label, not an identity: the same profile can be "Bob Nguyen" today and "Alex Nguyen" next week, and gating on it would refuse a correct send. Pass it when you have it: it is recorded as name_matched, and it becomes the DECIDING guard whenever the thread id could not be verified. A mismatch alone no longer aborts a send whose id checked out.
inputs.recipient_id: string (optional) — override the id to verify against; defaults to the id in thread_url
inputs.dry_run: bool (optional) — resolve + verify the recipient WITHOUT sending

capabilities.coverage: the logged-in operator messages as themselves

_impl.screen: messenger thread (messenger.com/e2ee/t/<vanity_or_id> preferred; facebook.com/messages/t/<id> still accepted)
_impl.method: DOM automation (gql_actions.js), guards in order, and NOTHING is typed until they pass: (0) the url must be a thread url; (1) read the id out of the address BEFORE touching the E2EE gate — that is the only moment it still exists, because passing the gate rewrites the address to /e2ee/t/<thread_id>; (2) click the "Continue" gate when present, then require EXACTLY ONE composer matching /^write to (.+)$/; (3) if the id could not be verified, the name must match (and with neither id nor name there is nothing left to prove identity, so it refuses). Then type via execCommand insertText (Lexical) and submit with Enter; verify the composer emptied AND the text appeared.
_impl.why_id_not_name: A display name is a label the recipient can change at will — the same profile is "Bob Nguyen" today and "Alex Nguyen" next week — so a name guard eventually refuses correct sends and trains the operator to switch it off. The profile id in the url is stable, and checking it before the gate also catches the real failure: when Messenger cannot resolve an id it quietly falls back to the inbox or another thread, and the requested id vanishes from the address.
_impl.why_messenger_com: messenger.com/e2ee/t/ accepts a VANITY (no numeric-id lookup first), is a dedicated surface with no docked chat heads to make the composer count ambiguous, and titles the tab "<Name> | Messenger" — a third, independent read on the recipient alongside the id and the composer's aria-label. Verified live on the vanity thaian.nguyen.731572 and the profile id 100026030446486.
_impl.why_not_the_profile_route: Clicking Message on a profile leaves several "Write to <someone>" composers in the DOM at once (the target plus every docked chat head), and the profile page does not expose its owner name (h1 is "Notifications") — there is no reliable way to tell them apart, so a profile url is rejected outright as not_a_thread_url.
_impl.validated_on: 2026-08-15 live on messenger.com: vanity thaian.nguyen.731572 sent (done/verified, id_verified, title agreed); profile id 100026030446486 accepted with NO recipient_name (id_verified=true); a photo id refused with composers_found=0; a wrong name on an unverifiable id refused with nothing typed
_impl.audit: result appended to outbox/actions_log.jsonl by the bridge

capabilities.title: Publish a new post into a Facebook group
capabilities.when_to_use: WRITE ACTION. Publish a standalone post into a group the acting account is a MEMBER of. Submit the GROUP url (facebook.com/groups/<id>) — not a permalink, and never a profile url, which would post to the operator's own timeline. This is the most exposed write the collector has: a comment sits under someone else's post, a DM is private, but a post stands alone in front of the whole group and is what members report as spam. Keep the daily cap low (agency settings: posts_per_account_per_day, default 2) and never push the same text into several groups on the same day. Approval is handled upstream by the daily report.

inputs.group_url: string (required) — https://www.facebook.com/groups/<id>. A permalink or profile url is refused (not_a_group_url), and the group landed on must match the one requested (group_mismatch).
inputs.dry_run: bool (optional) — open the composer and report whether the Post button is present, WITHOUT publishing

capabilities.coverage: the logged-in operator posts as themselves via the real UI

_impl.method: DOM automation (gql_actions.js). A group page shows a TRIGGER ("Write something..."), not a composer: click it, wait for the [role=dialog] that contains a contenteditable, require EXACTLY ONE such dialog (several open composers mean the page is not in the state we think it is), type via execCommand insertText, then submit by clicking the "Post" BUTTON — Enter only inserts a newline in this composer, unlike the comment box. Verify BOTH that the dialog closed AND that the text is on the page.
_impl.approval_states: A group may hold member posts for an admin to approve. The result distinguishes done (published) from pending_admin_approval (submitted, not visible yet). Never treat the second as the first: it would tell the operator something is live when it is queued.
_impl.guards: not_a_group_url · group_mismatch (landed on a different group) · no composer trigger (the account may not be a member, or posting is admin-only) · ambiguous_composer (more than one composer dialog) · text typed but no Post button found (reported explicitly — the text was NOT submitted)

scroll_contract: SCROLL CONTRACT: a capability scrolls ONLY when it declares max_scroll in its inputs. Everything else must not be scrolled by the runner; some of those still paginate, but via max_pages cursor replay, which is not scrolling. Scrolling a single-surface job (for example reading a published contact address) fires GraphQL queries whose results are discarded, costs time, and widens the request footprint for nothing.
